entries.name: Carbon
entries.whatItDoes: Carbon is discovery and evidence infrastructure for Physics AI: miners/researchers submit reproducible model-building recipes for fast physics surrogate models (battery fast charging first; cold plates, motors, photonics planned), and independent evaluators rebuild and test candidates against reference physics. Status: development/testnet only - no production rewards pay out yet.
entries.hardwareRec: Not specified in repo; recipe-based model building is largely CPU/scientific-Python work with challenge-dependent compute. Battery/CFD studies may want a GPU; the hosted battery journey is still an integration milestone, so treat this as a research rig until launch requirements land.
keyRequirements: Submit reproducible construction recipes within the challenge's supported vocabulary (constrained recipe format initially)
Mandatory physical checks must pass - high average accuracy cannot cancel a physics failure
Official evaluation cases remain separate from miner practice data
Work through Miner Control Center (browser UI) or Miner MCP for campaigns and submissions
As of Sep 2026: development + testnet only; publications are non-paying demonstrations
entries.minerJob: A miner selects a challenge (battery fast charging is the launch focus), explores methods with the Control Center/MCP tooling and public research material, runs permitted experiments, and crafts a frozen, reproducible model-building recipe. Evaluators rebuild the candidate in a pinned environment and compare predictions against reference physics with mandatory checks. Reward direction is planned winner-plus-burn via Alpha buyback, but implementation is outstanding - today the work is research positioning for launch, not live income.
minerJobProvide: Reproducible fast-physics model recipes (battery charging/ageing first)
Candidates passing mandatory physical validity checks
Research contributions via Control Center / Miner MCP
Evidence-grade methods ready for production challenges at launch
entries.top10Strategy: Position for launch: build genuine battery-modeling (electrochemical surrogate) capability now, engage with the repo's development studies, and be ready the moment paying challenges open. Because evaluators rebuild everything, reproducibility discipline and physics validity - not benchmark gaming - are the durable edge.
top10Levers: Deep battery simulation/ageing expertise - the first launch challenge
Recipe reproducibility under pinned evaluation environments
Watch PROJECT_STATUS.md and challenge-readiness docs for launch timing
Use Miner MCP early to integrate agents into your research loop
Respect physics-mandatory checks over raw accuracy
Customer-facing evidence products (Evidence Audit) as a parallel lane
entries.followTopMiners: Track carbonphysics.ai and the repo's PROJECT_STATUS.md for launch milestones, taostats.io/subnet/116 once rewards go live, and the carbonphysicsai/Carbon commit cadence (very active).

entries.name: Targon
entries.gpu: 8× H100 SXM / H200 / B200 / B300 / RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (TEE hardware profiles)
entries.whatItDoes: Targon is a confidential decentralized AI cloud: miners contribute TEE-capable GPU servers (Intel TDX / NVIDIA Confidential Compute) that host verifiable AI inference and compute for customers. Emissions are auction-based per GPU card with USD-denominated target prices, so miners earn by keeping attested cards live; emission not allocated to auctions is burned.
entries.hardwareRec: Bare-metal 8-GPU node: H100 SXM/H200/B200/B300 or RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Intel TDX CPU (TEE in BIOS), 128+ threads, 1.5-1.9 TiB RAM, 3 TB storage. TargonOS wipes all disks; clusters must be TEE-attested, so generic rentals don't qualify.
keyRequirements: TEE-capable hardware: Intel TDX (AMD SEV-SNP roadmap) with Confidential Compute enabled in BIOS
Exact 8-GPU profile (h100-8x, h200-8x, b200-8x, b300-8x, rtx-pro-6000-blackwell-8x); min cluster size 8 cards
Install signed TargonOS (wipes disks, auto-attests every boot); report node IPs in miner config.json
Run the miner (docker compose) with registered hotkey, external IP, and axon port 7777
Emissions pay per card up to the auction max_price cap; unallocated emission is burned
entries.minerJob: The miner installs TargonOS, a signed OS that on every boot attests to the Targon network, mounts encrypted LUKS storage, and starts Targon services. The miner daemon (docker-compose) registers each node's IP and axon on-chain so validators and the Targon scheduler can direct confidential inference workloads into the TDX VMs. Emissions are paid per card per hour against auctions (e.g. H200 target ~$2.90/hr, B200 ~$4.20/hr) with a max-price cap; once an auction passes its card target the pool spreads and per-card rates settle toward target. Rewards flow automatically per live, attested card.
minerJobProvide: TEE-attested 8-GPU compute nodes running confidential workloads
Always-on axon endpoint reporting live node inventory
Verifiable remote attestation each boot (secure boot, encrypted storage)
Capacity for confidential model inference (CC/PPCIE isolation)
entries.top10Strategy: Fleet operations, not ML: secure cheap TEE-capable hardware, keep every card attested and online 24/7, and watch the auctions API to add card types whose target price beats your power+colo cost. Top miners run multiple 8-GPU nodes per cluster, automate provisioning with iPXE netboot, and never let attestation or the miner daemon lapse.
top10Levers: Buy/colo TEE-capable servers early; per-auction card targets are limited
iPXE unattended TargonOS installs to scale fleets quickly
Zero attestation failures - no attestation means no emission
Keep config.json node IPs current and axon reachable
Compare your per-card payout on stats.targon.com miner stats

entries.name: iota
entries.whatItDoes: IOTA (Macrocosmos) pretrained LLMs across a swarm of heterogeneous machines: an orchestrator distributes model layers to miners and streams activations between them over a shared S3 bucket. Miners compete to process the most activations; validators spot-check that work was genuinely done. Currently training a 1.5B Llama-architecture model, with 15B-100B runs planned.
entries.hardwareRec: CUDA GPU >=16GB VRAM (RTX 4090 cited by repo), Ubuntu 22.04. bf16 footprint ~2GB per 1B params today; larger planned runs will raise the bar. One GPU joins a pipeline stage; README silent on rental marketplaces.
keyRequirements: CUDA GPU >=16GB VRAM (RTX 4090 example)
Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy)
uv + bash setup.sh, then .env config
Sustained connectivity to orchestrator and shared S3
Run under PM2 for reliability
entries.minerJob: You run start_miner.sh: the miner registers with the orchestrator, receives its assigned model layers, and streams activations for forward/backward passes. Miners race to process as many activations as possible each training stage, periodically upload local weights, and merge activations via a Butterfly All-Reduce variant. Validators spot-check miners to confirm assigned work was performed as required; emission flows per verified processing contribution across the multi-week run.
minerJobProvide: Processed activation batches per training step
Correct local weight updates uploaded on schedule
Butterfly All-Reduce merge contributions
Uptime across long uninterrupted training runs
entries.top10Strategy: Throughput-plus-reliability race: rewards track activations processed without failing spot-checks, so a pegged GPU, fast network path to orchestrator/S3, and zero downtime beat raw clock speed alone. Newcomers: follow the official IOTA mining setup guide exactly, monitor the public dashboard, and fix disconnects fast — every missed stream is lost paid work.
entries.followTopMiners: Watch iota.macrocosmos.ai/dashboard/mainnet for miner counts and run metrics, taostats.io/subnet/9 for top UIDs and incentive spread, docs.macrocosmos.ai for setup-guide changes, and the repo commit cadence for run upgrades.

entries.name: ChipForge
entries.whatItDoes: ChipForge is a digital-design competition subnet: on-chain challenges ask for Verilog/SystemVerilog implementations of real silicon components (AI accelerators, cryptographic modules, mini-GPUs). Miners download specs, design with AI assistance, and submit solutions; validators evaluate with industry EDA tools. It is winner-takes-all per challenge, feeding designs toward manufacturable chips.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU-heavy EDA work: synthesis/simulation/timing runs are CPU-bound (validators want 16-24 physical cores plus 32-48GB RAM); miners need a solid multicore box for local test loops. No GPU. The bare-metal note concerns state persistence in ./data, not a rental ban.
keyRequirements: Hotkey registered on netuid 108; repo stays on Bittensor 10.x (axon networking layer)
Miner polls the challenge server (default 300s) for spec/testbench packages; solutions are ZIPs of .v/.sv files
Winner-takes-all scoring with MIN_IMPROVEMENT_PERCENT margins; byte-identical copies refused
Winning designs are revealed to registered hotkeys after a set time (study them)
Leaderboard at chipforge.io/leaderboard shows the score to beat and every submission
entries.minerJob: Run start_miner.sh (or make up ROLE=miner): the miner polls the challenge server, downloads the challenge package (spec plus testbench), you design and locally verify Verilog/SystemVerilog against the testbench with your own Verilator/Yosys loop, then submit via miner_cli.py. Validators batch-evaluate with EDA tools (Verilator, Yosys, Icarus, Openlane) and reach consensus scores; the best design per challenge takes the emission.
minerJobProvide: Functionally correct, high-scoring Verilog/SystemVerilog designs per challenge
ZIP submissions passing validator test benches
Improvements beating the current winner by the required margin
Design reuse via the revealed-winners program
entries.top10Strategy: Winner-takes-all means only the #1 design per challenge is paid - breadth loses, depth in one challenge family (e.g. cryptographic modules) wins. Download revealed winning designs to calibrate against the evaluation bar, build a tight local EDA regression loop, and submit only when you beat the posted score-to-beat. Hardware-design skill is the moat; AI coding tools help but testbench-passing silicon thinking wins.
top10Levers: Deep design skill in one challenge family
Studying revealed winning designs (registered hotkeys only)
Fast response to newly announced challenges
entries.followTopMiners: Watch chipforge.io/leaderboard (current winner, per-submission consensus scores), TatsuProject repo commit cadence, and the ChipForge Discord channel for validator/EDA server updates.

entries.name: KubeTEE
entries.whatItDoes: KubeTEE is the AI Factory: miners run confidential (TEE) Kubernetes clusters serving enterprise AI services - SOTA inference via a LiteLLM gateway plus batch fine-tune/eval jobs - with hardware-level attestation (Intel TDX, NVIDIA CC). Validators score infrastructure readiness and USD-competitive pricing against Targon/Lium/Chutes; demand-side paid jobs land in Phase 2.
entries.hardwareRec: Datacenter cluster: 7+ nodes with 2-3 dedicated 8-GPU workers per type (H100/H200/B200/B300), Intel TDX BIOS-enabled, HA control plane, 100 TAO collateral deposit. Early Access onboarding is hand-reviewed; TEE-attested bare metal beats any generic rental.
keyRequirements: TEE attestation mandatory (Intel TDX/SGX + NVIDIA CC; Kata + CoCo runtime classes) - no attestation, no emissions
7 nodes minimum per cluster (5 combined control/etcd/worker, 3 dedicated 8-GPU workers per GPU type), one datacenter, one cluster per hotkey
Rancher inventory passing infra-readiness policy: readiness, HA topology, 8-GPU passthrough wiring, confidential runtime handler
100 TAO registration collateral on the mining hotkey (not slashable; emission stops and capital freezes on breach)
Hand-reviewed Early Access onboarding; KubeTEE binds the cluster via kubetee.ai/hotkey label + Rancher Fleet
USD price card per GPU-hour (H100 $4 / H200 $5.50 / B200 $8 / B300 $10 / RTX6000 $2.50), clamped by Targon SN4 payouts
entries.minerJob: A miner operates a TEE-hardened RKE2 Kubernetes cluster enrolled via Rancher Fleet; KubeTEE applies the hotkey binding and GitOps-deploys the stack (GPU Operator, Kata/CoCo, Longhorn, NeMo, monitoring). The cluster serves confidential inference through the LiteLLM gateway and will host Armada-scheduled batch jobs. Each epoch the validator enumerates nodes via Rancher, computes a binary infrastructure-readiness verdict plus a USD-denominated compensation weight, and sets weights on-chain. Emission flows per proven, priced capacity; unearned share recycles to unissued supply, never to the owner key.
minerJobProvide: TEE-attested multi-node Kubernetes cluster (RKE2, Kata/CoCo, NVIDIA CC)
HA topology with 8-GPU workers and GPU passthrough, passing readiness policy
Confidential inference capacity behind the LiteLLM gateway
Armada-ready batch job execution (fine-tune, eval) as demand lands
entries.top10Strategy: Enterprise-grade ops is the game: nail TDX + CC attestation, HA topology, and 8-GPU passthrough on day one, keep readiness perpetually green (the gate is binary - any gap zeroes your score), and stay priced at/below the rate card versus Targon payouts. Onboarding is demand-driven, so engage the team early and study BTLABS (UID 97), the reference production cluster.
top10Levers: Source turnkey TDX/NVIDIA-CC hardware - rare capability, early movers win slots
Binary readiness gate: hotkey binding, Rancher readiness, HA, passthrough all green
Price per GPU-hour at/below the card vs the Targon SN4 feed
Watch the Hippius-hosted validator dashboard for your scoring
Study BTLABS (UID 97) production path as the template
Uptime discipline: outages freeze reliability counters, never guessed through

entries.name: NOVA
entries.gpu: 2× GPUs with >48 GB VRAM each (Boltz-2 inference)
entries.whatItDoes: NOVA does high-throughput ML-driven drug screening: miners run Boltz-2 and BoltzGen inference to score binding/affinity and generate candidate compounds across huge chemical spaces. Pharma researchers get cheap screening at a fraction of normal cost; miners with serious GPUs earn by completing validator scoring rounds reliably and on time.
entries.hardwareRec: 2x GPUs each >48GB VRAM for parallel Boltz-2 inference - a single GPU runs sequentially and risks delayed/missing scoring rounds. CUDA 12.6, Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.10-3.12, ample RAM. A100/H100-class or 48GB+ pro cards; rental A100/H100 viable. Tune with tools/calibrate_perf.py.
keyRequirements: 2 GPU devices with >48GB VRAM each (parallel inference; one GPU = sequential = missed rounds)
CUDA 12.6 environment; clone with --recurse-submodules for the Boltz stack
GitHub personal access token with repo access for your submission repository
Tuned env: NOVA_BOLTZ_SHARDS, NOVA_BOLTZ_GPUS mapping, NOVA_MAX_CONCURRENT_TNP
Missing or delayed scoring rounds directly cost rewards
entries.minerJob: Operate neurons/miner.py continuously: validators dispatch compound-screening batches; the miner runs Boltz-2 structure/co-folding inference (shard processes spread across 2 GPUs) plus BoltzGen generation, returns candidate scores, and commits submissions to a GitHub repo the validators read. Rewards flow from completing each scoring round within the window - throughput and round-completion rate drive weights, so GPU sharding and uptime are the job.
minerJobProvide: Boltz-2 binding/affinity scores for validator-sent compound batches
BoltzGen candidate generation for chemical-space exploration
GitHub-hosted submission artifacts via scoped PAT
On-time completion of every scoring round
entries.top10Strategy: Throughput and reliability win: rewards hinge on finishing rounds fast, so GPU sharding via calibrate_perf.py, pinned drivers, and uptime dominate. Two 48GB+ cards are effectively mandatory - single-GPU setups run sequentially and miss rounds. Newcomers should rent A100/H100-class hardware rather than consumer cards and verify a full round completes inside the window before scaling up.
entries.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnets/68 top UIDs and round consistency, metanova-labs/nova commit cadence (inference version changes shift performance), and open repo issues or contact the NOVA team for validator API keys.

entries.name: Quasar
entries.whatItDoes: Quasar Training is decentralized pretraining: miners continue training the Quasar MoE model (Quasar Preview) toward 10T+ additional tokens. A subnet-run orchestrator splits model tensors into 24 fragments, assigns training leases, merges validator-approved live fragments, and releases public checkpoints. Buyers are the SILX team/ecosystem wanting decentralized training throughput.
entries.hardwareRec: Multi-GPU training node. Repo shows QUASAR_MINER_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 with FSDP on multi-GPU systems; treat this as a datacenter-class training rig (multiple large-VRAM GPUs). No TEE/static-IP requirement documented; OOM discipline and batch-size control matter.
keyRequirements: Registered native ED25519 hotkey on netuid 24
Latest miner release (signed live fragment claims + live-control grants)
Multi-GPU node; keep one hotkey on one machine only
Public S3 bucket reads (QUASAR_S3_ANONYMOUS=true) for run discovery
Steady training uptime so the syncer can pull live fragments
entries.minerJob: The miner publishes a heartbeat, discovers the active run, polls for jobs, verifies orchestrator signatures, decrypts scoped grants, downloads checkpoint/data via presigned URLs, and trains its assigned Quasar fragment. While training it answers live fragment pull requests (fragment_id = global_step % 24) with signed live claims and applies synced fragments the orchestrator pushes back. Validators verify claims against the frozen previous fragment state, evaluate quality, and approve merges; weights come only from accepted live merge events with decay - self-reported TPS, loss, and GPU names are telemetry only. Not winner-take-all: every accepted merge counts.
minerJobProvide: Validator-approved live fragment merges (the reward path)
Signed training artifacts and receipts for audit
Continuous fragment availability during training
Checkpoint-coverage contributions across the 24 fragments
entries.top10Strategy: Rewards follow accepted live-merge events, so the win condition is raw verified GPU-hours: stay online 24/7 on the latest release, keep FSDP/batch settings from OOMing, and respond to fragment pulls fast. Invalid, stale, replayed, or unsigned claims score zero. Newcomers should join via the published checkpoint manifest and target consistently high accepted-merge rates rather than one big run.
top10Levers: Fast live-fragment claim responses to syncer pulls
Staying current with miner releases (protocol changes)
entries.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnet/24 weights and rewarded miners; orchestrator current-run metadata and merge ledger via the public bucket; repo releases for protocol bumps; HuggingFace silx-ai/Quasar-Preview checkpoint cadence.

entries.name: Herald
entries.whatItDoes: A verified media-placement subnet: PR firms and contributors publish editorial articles in real news outlets against briefs. Validators run a code-only verification oracle checking each article on the outlet's own page (signed registry, brief window, topic match, not-paid-content, text match) and weight the contributor's hotkey by verified USD value; uncovered emission burns.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU only — in fact no miner server at all. The real 'hardware' is PR placement: you need real outlets willing to publish on-brief editorial content. Hotkey is registered through the Herald website with a wallet extension.
keyRequirements: Register hotkey on netuid 69 via Herald website
Google sign-in + wallet extension (Talisman/SubWallet/Polkadot.js)
Upload article text BEFORE publishing
Add live link; outlet must be in the signed registry
Article must stay live through a 30-day vesting window
Miner neuron deprecated — no server needed
entries.minerJob: There is no miner service: contributors register a hotkey on the website, pick an open brief (topic, optional date window, prepaid reward pool), upload the draft before publication, then add the published link. Once per daily epoch each validator verifies signatures, coldkey-hotkey ownership, outlet-registry membership, timing, topic, text match and paid-content status. Verified articles vest value by outlet tier and search presence in daily installments over 30 days; removal or conversion to paid content forfeits the rest. Emissions flow to your hotkey pro rata to payable USD.
minerJobProvide: Verified editorial articles in real outlets
On-brief topic coverage
Pre-publication signed text uploads
30-day article persistence
Registered hotkey earning emission shares
entries.top10Strategy: Rewards scale with outlet tier and search presence, so placement quality beats article count — one high-tier placement in a pooled brief can outweigh many low-tier posts. Choose briefs with prepaid pools and less competition, keep articles live for the full 30-day vest, and never let outlets tag them as paid. When contributor value exceeds the day's emission it's shared pro rata.
entries.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/69 weight distribution and the burn share, the Herald website brief board for open campaigns, docs/miner.md changes, and repo release cadence (spec version bumps).

entries.name: Ingot
entries.whatItDoes: Distil (SN97, formerly branded Albedo) is a king-of-the-hill competitive model-distillation subnet. The teacher is moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 (1T total / ~32B active MoE; Qwen3.5/3.6 teacher cutover went live 2026-05-02). Miners distill <=33B students, upload to HuggingFace and commit on-chain; validators score a 25+ axis composite; winner takes 100% of emissions.
entries.hardwareRec: Student-side bf16 training of 33B-class students: 4-8× H100/H200; LoRA + checkpointing fits smaller rigs. 2× 24GB only for sub-2B sanity runs. Quantized students (GPTQ/AWQ/GGUF) rejected. Training infra is your choice; rentals allowed, evaluation runs on validator GPUs.
keyRequirements: Kimi-family architecture + Kimi BPE tokenizer (vocab 163,840), <=33B total params, safetensors bf16/fp16
One PERMANENT commitment per hotkey (new attempts need a new hotkey)
Unique weights: SHA256 + activation-fingerprint near-copy detection
Model stays public and unchanged on HF — edits = DQ
Ranking key: composite.final = 0.75 × worst-3-axis mean + 0.25 × weighted mean
entries.minerJob: Train a distilled student, run test_miner.py (the same 15 validator checks locally), then commit the HF repo link on-chain (miner.py, dry-run first). Each commitment is scored exactly once: 11 procedurally-generated block-seeded axes (~50% — math, code, reasoning, long-context, knowledge, honesty), distillation tier (~30% incl. on-policy RKL), judge/quality and discipline axes. The king is re-evaluated every round on the same items; a challenger dethrones only at a 5% margin. Weight 1.0 to the king, 0 to everyone else.
minerJobProvide: Distilled <=33B Kimi-family student on a public HF repo
Permanent on-chain commitment per hotkey
High worst-3-axis composite (no weak-axis camping)
All 15 pre-submission checks passed before committing
entries.top10Strategy: Winner-take-all research problem: because 75% of the score is your three WORST axes, balanced students beat specialists — fix your weakest capability, don't polish KL. Newcomers: use on-policy RKL training (community script in examples/), pre-check everything locally to save registration burns, and budget for multiple hotkey attempts since commitments can't change.
top10Levers: Balanced quality across all axes (worst-3 rule)
Robustness to procedural block-seeded axes (no overfitting)
entries.followTopMiners: Watch distil.arbos.life (composite scores, king) and api.arbos.life, chat.arbos.life to query the current king, docs/MINER_FAQ.md and reports/ in the repo for axis changes, and taostats.io/subnet/97 for weight flips.

entries.name: 404—GEN
entries.whatItDoes: 404-GEN runs a decentralized 3D-generation competition: miners generate 3D models from published seeds/prompts, validators compare them in VLM pairwise duels, and winners are audited by regenerating outputs from the miner's Docker image on serverless GPUs. Anyone needing AI-generated 3D assets is the buyer; the best pipeline wins each round.
entries.hardwareRec: Multi-GPU rig for 3D model training/generation - audits regenerate on 4xH200 serverless pods using the hardware you declare in hardware.json. A single H100/H200-class node can compete; CPU-only cannot. Workload ships as Docker, so cloud GPUs are fine.
keyRequirements: Register on-chain during the OPEN window; generate from the published seed and prompts before the deadline
Upload 3D files (Three.js JS modules) to your own CDN for validators to download
Provide a Docker image that reproduces outputs; winners are regenerated on serverless GPUs (4xH200 default)
Outputs are statically analyzed, sandboxed, rendered via headless Chromium, then VLM-judged
Regenerated outputs must match submission quality (DINOv3 perceptual-distance checks)
entries.minerJob: Each round the miner pulls the published seed and prompts, runs its 3D-generation pipeline, uploads models to its CDN, and registers on-chain while the round is OPEN. Validators download submissions, render multi-view PNGs, and run VLM pairwise duels; candidate winners are verified by regenerating outputs from their Docker image on a serverless 4xH200 pod (128 prompts in 4 batches, same seed). The round winner becomes leader; repeated leader wins suffer weight decay toward a floor while new winners start at weight 1.0.
minerJobProvide: Generated 3D assets from published seeds/prompts, uploaded to your CDN
On-chain registration within the round's block window
A reproducible Docker image that regenerates your outputs exactly
Round-winning pipeline that survives VLM duels and audit
entries.top10Strategy: Winner-stays-in: you must beat the reigning leader decisively every round, and one-off wins decay. Build a fast, deterministic pipeline that handles the whole prompt pool, keep generation inside the block windows, and guarantee your Docker reproduces outputs - audit failures discard the win. Mine the public round state files to learn which styles win duels.
top10Levers: Prompt diversity: one pipeline must cover the entire round prompt pool
Determinism with the round seed - regeneration must match submissions
Inference speed: generation deadlines are block-limited
Study public state (leader.json, matches_matrix.csv) for VLM judge preferences
Keep GitHub Actions Docker builds green - build failure forfeits audit
Strike when the champion's weight has decayed
entries.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/17 top UIDs plus leader transitions, the public competition state repo (leader.json, per-round winner files in 404-Repo org), and the Bittensor Discord 404-GEN channel for competition/config changes.

entries.name: DaniLabs
entries.whatItDoes: Inference Labs' Proof-of-Inference subnet: builds zk-ML verification so an AI prediction can be proven to come from a specific model. Miners produce verifiable predictions plus zero-knowledge proofs; validators verify proofs and score them. It earns by supplying verifiable-inference infrastructure - trust-minimized AI outputs for buyers who cannot trust a black-box API.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU-only per README: 8-core 3.2GHz+ (3.6GHz+ competitive), 32-64GB RAM, 400Mbps-1Gbps symmetric network, 1-2TB NVMe SSD. zk-proving is CPU-heavy; faster CPU/network/storage directly raises rewards. Rented cloud VMs are fine; no GPU required.
keyRequirements: Run the sn2-miner Rust binary (prebuilt release, Docker image, or build from source)
Registered hotkey on netuid 2 (finney); PM2 or Docker+watchtower recommended
Score = cryptographic integrity, time-to-proof, proof size, and response time
Binaries auto-update every 5 minutes with atomic replacement - do not fight it
HTTP (port 8091) and QUIC (btlightning) endpoints reachable
entries.minerJob: Runs the sn2-miner Rust daemon over HTTP/QUIC. Validators push input data; the miner runs its custom verifiable model - an AI model compiled into a zero-knowledge circuit - and returns the prediction plus a zk proof. Validators verify proofs via the Expander backend and weight miners on proof size, generation time, and response latency. Rewards flow purely from Yuma weights on those performance metrics, so better proving hardware and efficiency mean higher weight. Prebuilt binaries self-update every 5 minutes.
minerJobProvide: Verified AI predictions returned to validator requests
A zero-knowledge proof of inference per prediction (Expander-compatible)
Fast time-to-proof (scored directly)
Compact proofs (proof size is scored)
High-uptime HTTP and QUIC endpoints
entries.top10Strategy: This is a systems/efficiency race, not a model-quality race: winners minimize proof time, proof size, and response latency on strong bare-metal CPUs and 1Gbps+ links. A newcomer breaks top-10 by over-provisioning CPU clock, NVMe, and network, keeping the binary current via auto-update, and watching the stats dashboard to see where the proof-latency frontier sits - every performance point is scored.
top10Levers: CPU clock speed and core count for faster proving
1Gbps+ symmetric network to cut response latency
Track sn2-stats.inferencelabs.com and wandb for frontier metrics
entries.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/2 top UIDs and incentive spread, the sn2-stats.inferencelabs.com dashboard and wandb.ai/inferencelabs/subnet-2 for proof-latency distributions, and GitHub release cadence on inference-labs-inc/subnet-2.

entries.name: TrajectoryRL
entries.whatItDoes: TrajectoryRL Season 2 pits miners against each other on 'fusion policies' - programs that decide, per request, which of eight open-weight models on Engy answer an agent and in what combination. Validators run scenario containers with hidden tests; the best policy holds the seat and is served on Engy as engy/auto for paying customers.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU only - explicitly 'no GPU, no server, no uptime': the platform stores your pack and validators run everything. Your real cost is model-call spend for local evaluation against your own Engy API key.
keyRequirements: Pack containing SKILL.md plus policy.json, policy.py (small SDK), or an OpenAI-compatible server
Policy may only call the eight allowlisted Engy models; $0.30 per-scenario spend cap

entries.name: Ormas
entries.whatItDoes: Ormas pays for accepted outcomes, not inference turns. A client describes a code change plus the acceptance test that proves it; miners offer firm or limit prices for the whole task, deliver the change, and are paid only when validators re-run the acceptance tests successfully. It is an outcome-priced decentralized coding marketplace on Bittensor.

Agents reach reasoning models and Numinous Signals/Indicia through a signing gateway; usage is billed to the miner. At resolution, S = (prediction - target)^2 - (market_price - target)^2 is scored against the market price 7 days later; rewards split by how far ahead of the field you finish.

Coverage across at least 85% of live events
Deterministic, reproducible agent behavior across validators

entries.name: SOMA
entries.whatItDoes: SOMA (Dendrite) is a competition subnet for context compression: miners build algorithms and models that shrink AI-agent context (history, tool outputs, files) while preserving task success. Validators run real agent workloads with your compression enabled, scoring task quality and weighted token consumption against uncompressed baselines. Buyers: anyone running context-heavy agents.
entries.hardwareRec: Unspecified. Algorithmic compression is CPU-only; hybrid model-based approaches may want a modest GPU. The platform/validators execute workloads (their floor: 4 cores, 16GB RAM, 500GB SSD). You need a registered hotkey on netuid 114.
keyRequirements: Build a compression solution compatible with the active competition rules (miner/README_prompting.md)
Upload submissions to the SOMA platform, tied to your registered hotkey
Scored on task performance plus weighted token consumption vs uncompressed baseline
Quality preservation matters - compression that breaks previously-passing tasks fails
Consistency across tasks and repeated runs is scored
Cycle: submission window -> screening/qualification -> evaluation
entries.minerJob: Develop and upload compression solutions during submission windows: algorithmic (summarization, selection, structured state), model-based, or hybrids. The platform associates submissions with your hotkey, screens and qualifies them, then validators execute standardized agent workloads with your compression active - measuring whether agents still complete tasks while consuming fewer weighted tokens (input/cached/output priced differently). Aggregated rankings feed subnet weights. Between cycles you iterate on your weakest measured signal.
minerJobProvide: Compression solution compatible with the active competition
Token savings without task failures
Stable results across repeated runs
Platform-registered submission per hotkey
Iterative improvements across competition cycles
entries.top10Strategy: The objective is maximum useful compression, not maximum ratio. Study which token categories are weighted (cached input vs fresh) and design for real economic savings while keeping task success at baseline. Ship early in each submission window, use screening feedback, and iterate - quality preservation is where most entries die. Newcomers with strong summarization/prompt engineering can beat heavier model-based approaches.
top10Levers: Task-success preservation at high compression ratios

entries.name: StreetVision by NATIX

entries.name: Ralph
entries.whatItDoes: Ralph is a model-compression tournament on one pinned model (Qwen3-8B): compress it into four bit tiers (binary ~1.15, ternary 1.75, sub2 2.3, sub4 4.0 bits/weight) without changing the architecture. The best compression per tier - scored by downstream semantic-effect equivalence, three judges, worst-slice - becomes 'king', ships as public downloadable crown weights, and keeps 80% of the tier's reward.
entries.hardwareRec: No always-on box: compression is done privately offline; budget research GPU time (H100-class practical for 8B quantization experiments; the subnet-rented eval side references H100 80GB). One artifact per coldkey+tier per round.
keyRequirements: Commit-reveal on chain: commit exact served bytes before the round exists
Architecture/weight-element count must match Qwen/Qwen3-8B exactly
GGUF needs a mainline llama.cpp Metal path (TQ1_0/TQ2_0 banned)
Measured bits/weight (from tensor data) under the tier cap
Copies earn nothing; one owner per artifact bytes (earlier commit wins)
entries.minerJob: You compress Qwen3-8B privately (GPTQ, AWQ, bitsandbytes, or your own scheme), verify the bit budget with eval.bitrate, commit the content hash of exactly what you'll serve on-chain, then reveal when the round opens. Validators run six gates (economics, safety, tier fit, bit budget, pinned parent, commit-reveal), then score all submissions with three judges on exams drawn from the post-commit nonce: downstream-effect similarity to the pinned parent. The tier's king keeps 80%, the best challenger with a strictly positive paired margin gets 20%, everyone else gets nothing; crowns change hands at a 0.02 lead (0.01 in two consecutive rounds), and a three-round king defends against half margins.
minerJobProvide: Compressed Qwen3-8B artifacts per bit tier
On-chain commit-reveal of exact served bytes
Crown-beating compression (public king artifacts)
Pre-verified bit budget via eval.bitrate
entries.top10Strategy: Winner-take-most: start from the published crown in RalphLabsAI/ralph-crowns and genuinely improve it - copying scores the same as the original (zero margin) and earns nothing. Master the bit-budget rules (per-tensor mixing headroom: 1-bit body + 2-bit embedding measures 1.076) and avoid the TQ* trap. For binary tier, use published 1-bit PTQ frameworks (BiLLM, ARB-LLM) then export to Q1_0. Hash the downloaded repo, not local files - commit-reveal mismatch is the top rejection.
top10Levers: Novel PTQ methods (BiLLM/ARB-LLM for binary; imatrix schemes for sub2/sub4)
Worst-slice quality across all three judges, languages, depths
Commit hygiene (hash exactly what HF serves)
Persistence: contender seats carry into next rounds
entries.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnets/40; HuggingFace RalphLabsAI/ralph-v2-rounds (signed round records) and ralph-crowns (current kings); repo commits; eval.precheck to see the whole pending queue and competitors.

entries.name: UR
entries.whatItDoes: UR is a decentralized privacy network: network operators sell VPN/proxy traffic carried by independent providers. Validators walk server-assigned provider routes measuring liveness and latency; Yuma consensus turns those measurements into emission. Demand is revenue-backed - operators deposit alpha sized to real usage, which funds pool payouts to providers via Merkle claims.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU only; this is a bandwidth play. Providers run the UR client on residential/VPS hosts carrying ingress/egress traffic with stable connections and routable IPs. Fleets holding many distinct routable /29 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6) prefixes can reach the head tier.
keyRequirements: Register as a provider via a network operator (ur.xyz); pool tier needs no UID or burn
Run provider software carrying ingress/egress traffic under a registered client_id
Survive validator probes: Wilson-score liveness interval and latency p95/p99 (EMA-smoothed)
Head tier requires burn-registered UID, manifest commitment, dual-signed client bindings; 200-fleet cap
7-day settlement epochs; pool payouts claimed with Merkle proofs from the vault
entries.minerJob: Run the provider miner pointed at an operator's API; it carries VPN ingress/egress for that privacy network's customers. Each tempo validators measure your hops' liveness and latency; pools are weighted implied_usage x quality (clamped 0.75-1.0) and paid through Merkle claims, while top fleets ranked by routable-IP breadth get native Yuma payments straight to their hotkey. A client earns in exactly one tier at a time.
minerJobProvide: Real VPN/proxy ingress and egress bandwidth for privacy customers
Verified liveness (Wilson interval) and low p95/p99 latency on probed hops
Distinct routable egress prefixes for head-tier fleet breadth
Correct client_id attribution for Merkle pool claims
entries.top10Strategy: The pool tier is the on-ramp: quality is clamped so pools differ at most 1.33x, meaning uptime and latency dominate - join a strong operator and run stable bandwidth. The head pays natively but needs broad routable IP breadth, effectively for operators with many distinct /29s. Note the mainnet bootstrap weights 90% to owner hotkeys initially, so positioning with operators matters more than solo residential lines today.
top10Levers: Routable-IP breadth (distinct /29 or /48 prefix hashes) for head fleets
Early burn-registered head fleet UID (limited head slots)
Avoiding tier conflicts (client earns in exactly one tier)

entries.name: Vanta

entries.name: ChronoLLM
entries.whatItDoes: ChronoLLM pays miners to train small language models with strict temporal cutoffs - a 2018 model knows nothing after 2018 - removing lookahead bias for financial backtesting and historical analysis. TEE validators test leak behavior on private data, then run GPT-judged quality duels; the top 10 split emissions exponentially (#1 roughly 52%).

Validators on Phala Cloud (Intel TDX) run anti-copy, leak-detection, and qualification stages, then round-robin quality duels on fresh LLM-generated prompts judged by GPT-5.4; final ranking is quality win-rate among models that pass the leak gate. entries.name: GPUForge
entries.whatItDoes: GPUForge is a proposed subnet for verifiable GPU training work: a publisher signs immutable training-job manifests, miners execute them on eligible NVIDIA H100 hardware, and validators measure correct, useful training throughput (attestation, digests, canary challenges, tolerance-bounded correctness) and convert it into weights. Critically, the repo states it is NOT ready for miners, validators, testnet, or mainnet.
entries.hardwareRec: NVIDIA H100 (SXM/PCIe/NVL normalized); default policy requests 1 GPU with 81,920 MiB. NVIDIA NVAT hardware attestation is a planned gate, so attestation-capable hosting is implied. No supported miner release exists yet - do not provision production spend.
keyRequirements: None actionable today: 'no supported miner or validator release yet'

Never run untrusted publisher training jobs or use production wallets
When live: digest-pinned containers, least-privilege isolation, no outbound network
Hardware-backed H100 attestation (NVAT 1.x) expected as a verification tier
entries.minerJob: Once live (not today), the miner would report capabilities, accept validator-signed short-lived work leases, run the pinned publisher workload in a hardened isolated container, and return signed execution evidence: checkpoint commitments, challenge outputs, timing under throughput-plausibility envelopes. Validators verify NVAT attestation tiers, manifest identity, hidden commit-reveal canaries, randomized correctness probes, and anomaly bounds before weighting. Everything is layered evidence - no single measurement proves execution. Until testnet acceptance criteria are met, this is design documentation, not an operational miner.
minerJobProvide: Verified training throughput on H100 (future)
Signed execution evidence bundles
Checkpoint commitments matching declared cadence
Attestation-capable hosting posture
entries.top10Strategy: Prepare, don't spend: the README forbids production use, so the play is monitoring. Track the repo for the release announcement, testnet acceptance criteria, and attestation requirements; pre-qualify attested H100 hosting and hardened container ops. Subnets that launch with verifiable-training narratives typically reward early reliable operators, but entry only makes sense after the fail-closed gates ship.
top10Levers: Early testnet participation when releases land

Creators and businesses use it for affordable upscaling/compression; speed and quality tiers set rewards.

Validators benchmark by downscaling high-resolution videos for you to upscale and providing videos to compress; outputs are scored via VMAF (compression: full-video via Docker/libvmaf) and PIE-APP (upscaling), with speed/duration multipliers layered on quality. Organic user videos arrive chunked and queued — process and return them within service windows; consistency compounds through the tier multipliers.

entries.name: Minos
entries.whatItDoes: Minos is decentralized genomic variant calling: every 72 minutes the platform generates a challenge BAM with hidden synthetic mutations (HelixForge, injected at read level). Miners run variant callers on it and submit tuned hyperparameter configurations - never outputs. Validators execute each config independently and score results with hap.py; later stages open custom algorithm competitions.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU only per repo specs: miner >=4 cores / 8-16GB RAM (8GB BCFtools, 16GB DeepVariant), >=60GB disk (per-round BAMs ~6GB each), Docker required. Validators need 8 cores/32GB. Input metadata agrees (CPU-only, 0 VRAM).
keyRequirements: Docker 20.10+ (24.0+ recommended); Bittensor 10.3.1 (11.x unsupported)
72-minute cycles with lag scoring (submit cycle N while N+1 runs)
Submit configuration only - validators run it themselves
Parameter ranges enforced per tool template (GATK/DeepVariant/BCFtools; FreeBayes deprecated)
Demo mode (start-miner.sh --demo) to score without registering
entries.minerJob: Run the miner loop: poll the platform, download the cycle's challenge BAM via presigned URL (Hippius SN75 / Cloudflare R2 / S3 fallback), run your chosen variant caller with tuned parameters, and submit the hyperparameter configuration through your axon. Validators download configs, execute them against the challenge genome, and score with hap.py (industry-standard precision/recall) against the hidden mutations; weights come from round scores with winner-heavy pruning dust weights. The tuning game is systematic: tools have different strengths per genome region, and the accepted parameter space is documented in templates and docs/parameter_ranges.md.
minerJobProvide: Tuned variant-calling configs per 72-min cycle
High hap.py F1/precision on hidden mutations
Consistent cycle participation (lag-scored)
Clean config validation within parameter ranges
entries.top10Strategy: Hyperparameter-search quality wins early: automate Bayesian/Optuna-style sweeps per tool against local truth sets so your configs generalize to fresh genomes, and pick the right tool per challenge (DeepVariant vs GATK vs BCFtools trade speed for accuracy). Reliability across all cycles compounds rank history. When custom-algorithm stages open, first movers with novel pipelines take the ground.
top10Levers: Fast turnaround within the 72-min lag window

entries.name: Nepher Robotics

Buyers get benchmarked robotics policies and an evaluation harness.

entries.name: Aurelius
entries.whatItDoes: Aurelius is a moral-reasoning alignment subnet. Miners submit structured ethical-dilemma scenario configs; validators score them through an 8-stage pipeline (schema, rate-limit, novelty, classifier, simulation) and run accepted scenarios through DeepMind Concordia generative-agent simulations. Transcripts become training data that improves LLM performance on moral-reasoning benchmarks (MoReBench).
entries.hardwareRec: CPU-only for miners: a Docker host with a public IP (axon port 8091). The validator side uses an OpenAI-compatible LLM API (DeepSeek default, cheapest) instead of local GPUs. No GPU requirement found for miners; a small VPS is enough.

entries.minerJob: You run the aurelius-miner container serving operator-authored scenario JSONs from a configs/ directory in round-robin order, each stamped with a work_id and hotkey-signed via ScenarioConfigSynapse. The validator charges work tokens, pushes each config through the 8-stage pipeline including a Concordia simulation sidecar, and sets weights on outcomes. Miners never generate configs at request time — quality authoring happens offline and the container restarts to pick up additions.

Signed round-robin responses carrying work_id

Newcomers: study testlab configs in the aurelius-ops repo, author programmatically (seed_generator.py as reference), keep a large diverse library, and budget work tokens.

entries.name: Graphite
entries.whatItDoes: A decentralized network for graph optimization, currently focused on the Traveling Salesman Problem. Validators send synthetic TSP instances; miners return tours scored against the best cohort solution and a greedy benchmark. Aimed at logistics/routing use cases; a planned frontend will let users submit their own graph problems.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU only — TSP quality is algorithm work, not GPU work. The repo ships four starter algorithms (Nearest Neighbour, Dynamic Programming, Beam Search, Hybrid Pointer Network); custom high-performance solvers are the differentiator.
keyRequirements: Python miner per docs/miner.md

Beat the greedy benchmark or be penalized
Team warns of breaking changes — join Discord
entries.minerJob: Run the miner neuron from the Graphite repo; validators broadcast TSP instances and the miner returns high-quality tours computed by its solver. Scoring compares your tour length relative to the best solution in the cohort and a benchmark greedy heuristic; solutions falling short of the benchmark are penalized. Upgrading from the bundled heuristics to stronger solvers (better local search, or improved learned approaches like the provided pointer network) is how weight share is won.

entries.top10Strategy: This is an algorithms race: the bundled algorithms are the floor, not the ceiling — winners implement stronger TSP solvers (OR-tools/LKH-style local search or improved learned models) that reliably beat the greedy benchmark by a wide margin at low latency. Because scoring is relative to the cohort, small consistent margins across every instance compound into a dominant weight share.

Wide margin over the greedy benchmark

entries.name: Quantum Compute

Premium tiers: priority execution, extra shots, private off-chain execution
entries.minerJob: Miners are QPU operators: they receive validated quantum circuit jobs, execute them on their quantum hardware, and broadcast results back through the network for verification. entries.name: engy
entries.whatItDoes: engy serves frontier open-weight models on consumer GPUs with cryptographic verification: every response carries a TOPLOC activation fingerprint proving the pinned (Merkle-rooted) weights actually ran; a sampled recompute audit re-derives challenged matrix multiplies, and a failed opening is proof of cheating. Buyers pay engy.ai for completions; miners serve the traffic and earn subnet emissions.
entries.hardwareRec: 2x RTX 4090/5090, or 1x L40S / RTX 6000 Ada (48GB), or H100/H200/B200. Repo runbook has a working 4x RTX 4090 reference for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 via sglang. No TEE requirement - rented GPUs are workable.

MAX_INFLIGHT >= 8 (declared serve concurrency, the gateway minimum)

entries.minerJob: One process does everything: engy_miner.py connects to the gateway websocket, receives buyer completion requests routed for your declared model, generates via local sglang, and returns the completion plus a compact TOPLOC proof that the pinned model produced it. The gateway enforces the model's request-shape spec and your MAX_INFLIGHT; per-miner aggregates feed a master-signed epoch weight vector that light validators verify (sha256 digest + sr25519 signature) and resubmit on chain ~every 120 blocks. Rewards flow from verified serving volume in each epoch - more paid traffic served with valid proofs means more weight.

Scale concurrency well past the 8 minimum, keep GPUs saturated and sglang current, and hold near-perfect proof-pass rate - failed audits are cheating evidence, not bad luck. entries.name: Noah
entries.whatItDoes: Noah (built by Vora) is not a compute market - it is a financial-contribution subnet around 'the Ark'. Miners are scored on two on-chain facts: their eligible spendable NOAH earnings and their qualifying contributions to the Ark - ownership transfers of staked NOAH that arrive at the official Ark coldkey, delegated to the designated Ark Validator, and labeled with the miner's identity. The Noah Validator reads finalized chain records, computes a daily score per miner, and publishes weights. There is no model to serve, no queries to answer, and no work product: the 'product' is permanent capital contribution. Contributions transfer ownership and are not withdrawable.
entries.hardwareRec: Effectively nothing - CPU-only. No miner daemon or axon needs to be reachable and scoring is purely on-chain, so any cheap CPU VPS (1 vCPU / 1-2 GB RAM) or a laptop can run the Python deposit helper and hold keys. No GPU and no VRAM floor (platform floor: None (CPU-only)). The real cost is capital, not hardware: 10 NOAH entry contribution per hotkey, then an ongoing 50% of eligible spendable earnings contributed to the Ark.
keyRequirements: Register a hotkey on SN82 and make the entry contribution: 10 NOAH per miner hotkey
Contributions must arrive at the official Ark coldkey delegated to the designated Ark Validator - staking to the validator from your own wallet does NOT count
Every contribution must identify its miner (stable label) - an unnamed deposit receives no mining credit and is unrecoverable
Daily obligation: contribute 50% of eligible spendable earnings (newly spendable + earnings that unlock that day; returned registration collateral is not earnings)
Contributions transfer ownership to the Ark and are not withdrawable - treat every send as permanent
Use the deposit helper flow (preview -> send -> receipt) and verify against finalized chain records, never mempool state
entries.minerJob: Run nothing 24/7 - the daily job is treasury management with the noah-miner CLI: preview the fixed deposit (deposit --preview), send the reviewed deposit with a stable label (deposit --label entry), then read its receipt (status). Keep enough liquid NOAH to cover each day's 50% obligation on time, because the streak records whether each day's requirement was met - catching up later never rebuilds a missed day's streak. Advance contributions can pre-cover future days, and surplus first repays shortfalls before becoming uncapped advance coverage. Optionally audit published scores with noah.scoring.audit_published - 'AGREES' means the published score follows from the chain inputs under the checked-in scoring code.
minerJobProvide: Labeled ownership transfers of staked NOAH to the Ark (delegated to the Ark Validator)
Daily coverage of 50% of eligible spendable earnings, on time
Streak hygiene: no missed days; outages marked noFault only when genuinely fault-free
Receipt verification against finalized chain records
entries.top10Strategy: This is a capital-allocation game, not an engineering one - the top wallets are simply the ones that can afford to contribute the most capital permanently. On-target miners earn roughly a 1.0 contribution multiplier; surplus raises the PCI up to the 2.0 cap, which at the 50% target and harshness 2 needs a cumulative contribution ratio of about 70.71%. Score compounds credit x streak x slot x gate, and pay weight = integer_sqrt(score) x multiplier, so uninterrupted streaks and sustained surplus matter more than one big deposit. Weigh the structural risk before committing: deposits are irreversible, weights are set by a single designated scoring validator, and on-chain stake is heavily concentrated in a handful of wallets - so treat SN82 as speculation on contributed capital's token appreciation, not mining income.
top10Levers: Capital surplus: push the cumulative contribution ratio past ~70.7% to reach the 2.0 multiplier cap
Unbroken streaks: meet every day's 50% obligation on time - a missed day permanently breaks its streak
Advance coverage: pre-fund future days so outages never create a miss
Hold the minimum: if the holding gate closes, score is zero (mainnet profile minimum is currently 0)
Label every deposit: unnamed or misrouted transfers earn nothing and cannot be recovered

The validator recomputes rewards (mismatch = reject), gates groups on reward variance, ranks by std(rewards) x (1-mean(rewards)), proves top-down, and picks up to 16 winners per environment; winners accumulate and train. Generate high-variance, mid-difficulty prompt groups (they clear the variance gate and rank well), never mismatch seeds/profiles (WRONG_RANDOMNESS rejections), and reload new checkpoints instantly to avoid reject cycles. Today a temporary bridge pays equal weights to registered miners passing HTTPS health checks - translation scoring is not yet the reward path.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU-only accepted: the bridge phase only checks an HTTPS endpoint, and docs include Apple Silicon setup for model work. A lightweight keepalive qualifies now; real model serving needs modest compute, no GPU requirement stated.
keyRequirements: Registered SN78 hotkey with public IP and port announced on chain
Serve https://ANNOUNCED_IP:PORT/healthz - HTTP 200 within 5 seconds, response <=16KiB, no redirect
System-trusted TLS certificate valid for the announced IP (self-signed or hostname-only rejected)
UID must have no validator permit; UID 0 and owner-associated hotkeys excluded
Shared coldkey/IP/funding groups split equal weight among passing UIDs
Registration does not guarantee rewards - check the current quote and bridge rules
entries.minerJob: During the live bridge phase the miner's job is minimal: keep a registered hotkey with an announced IP/port and serve a healthz HTTPS endpoint passing validator health checks (5s response, trusted TLS for that IP). Weights are set per finalized row - every qualifying coldkey/IP/funding group gets equal total weight divided among its passing UIDs, refreshed before each write; failed endpoints get zero for that row. Open-competition intake is live, but accepted_no_weight receipts do not pay; the bridge is the current reward mechanism.
minerJobProvide: Always-on HTTPS /healthz endpoint (5s response, trusted TLS)
Stable announced IP and port on chain
Registered hotkey in good standing
Optional private or contributed ASL-translation model for the future competition
entries.top10Strategy: Right now this is an ops checklist, not a competition: equal weights mean every passing UID earns the same, so top-10 equals reliable infrastructure - static IP, valid TLS, uptime monitoring - plus multiple qualifying hotkeys within the shared-group rules. Build the real edge for when translation scoring activates: train and serve a strong ASL-to-English model now and follow docs/CURRENT_MINER_OPERATION.md closely, since bridge rules change without a sunset date.
top10Levers: Cheap VPS footprint during the health-check phase
Early ASL model and competition readiness

entries.name: MANTIS
entries.whatItDoes: MANTIS is 'The Ultimate Signal Machine': miners publish encrypted financial-prediction payloads (ETH direction, FX binaries, volatility paths, multi-asset breakouts, cross-sectional rankings, funding rates, FLOW bracket trades). Validators sample payloads every 5 blocks, decrypt after a Drand timelock matures, and score walk-forward salience into on-chain weights.
entries.hardwareRec: 1x RTX 4090 per input metadata, though signal generation is light (torch/scikit-learn); any reliable box producing payloads on cadence works. Real requirements are quant skill and, for FLOW challenges, posted on-chain capital.
keyRequirements: V2 JSON payloads on Cloudflare R2 (object key = your hotkey, <=25MB)
Dual-path encryption: owner X25519 + Drand IBE timelock (BLS12-381), binding hash AAD
Challenges weighted: MULTI-BREAKOUT 5.0, FUNDING-XSEC 4.0, ETH-LBFGS 3.5, XSEC-RANK 3.0
FLOW: post real bets on the FlowCollateralPool contract; t>=1.25 significance gate
BURN_PCT 0.35 to UID 0; uniqueness/anti-Sybil penalties on duplicates
entries.minerJob: Run your signal pipeline (generate_and_encrypt.py / flow_post.py are the supported surfaces): produce predictions/embeddings per challenge, encrypt dual-path so nobody sees them pre-maturation, and upload to R2. Validators decrypt via Drand after the window, store (embedding, price) pairs in SQLite, and compute walk-forward salience - L2 logistic/ElasticNet importance, top-K selection, uniqueness penalties for >85% argmax overlap, EMA smoothing (alpha 0.15) - then set weights. FLOW works differently: you post bracket trades (direction, Kelly fraction, stops) with your own collateral on-chain; cleared keys split the pool pro rata, uncleared keys get 2% dust, rest burns.
minerJobProvide: Timely encrypted prediction payloads every sampling window
Statistically salient signals (walk-forward AUC > 0.5)
De-correlated predictions (uniqueness penalties)
FLOW bracket trades with posted collateral
entries.top10Strategy: Genuine out-of-sample edge, not volume: salience is regression-coefficient importance, so de-correlated, unique signals beat clones (Sybil clones split weight; duplicates get zeroed). Concentrate skill on the high-weight challenges (BREAKOUT/FUNDING/LBFGS). FLOW needs real capital and a hard significance gate (t>=1.25 full-history or rolling) - post-sized bets, don't spray. The Model Iteration Tool repo is the sanctioned backtesting path.
top10Levers: True predictive edge on high-weight challenges
entries.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnets/123 weights (platform data: ~248/256 earned, broad distribution); MANTIS site settlement console (FLOW books, public recomputation); FLOW_RELEASE.pdf; repo MINER_GUIDE.md and Model Iteration Tool.

entries.name: Tag101
entries.whatItDoes: Tag101 is a decentralized semantic tagger for X/Twitter posts: miners transform posts into concise structured tags identifying entities, topics, and events. Validators score tags by consensus alignment (embedding clusters), validity (relevance plus format tiers), and diversity (non-redundancy). Downstream systems buy the structured signals for indexing and real-time topic tracking.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU only - the reference miner calls the OpenAI API (OPENAI_API_KEY, optional OPENAI_BASE_URL/MODEL overrides); Docker or PM2 on a small VPS. Rented GPU/cloud unnecessary; LLM spend is the cost.
keyRequirements: OpenAI API key (or OPENAI_BASE_URL/MODEL override) for the reference miner
Docker deployment recommended (built-in auto-update) or PM2 with a venv
Tags must be relevant, non-redundant, and well-formed (validity tiers 0/0.3/0.6/1.0)
Duplicate penalty: identical tag sets shared by many miners are sigmoid-penalized (k=0.1, c=50)
Tasks come from a whitelisted X account database (current season: AI-related accounts)
entries.minerJob: Run the SN101 miner container: it receives posts from validators, calls your configured LLM to emit a small tag set per post, and returns them. Each tag scores 0.6 x consensus (cluster support x centroid proximity) + 0.4 x validity x diversity, averaged per task; validator scoreboards aggregate recent task scores into relative miner scores for weights. Reward follows semantic alignment with the network's consensus reading of each post.
minerJobProvide: Concise structured tags per X post (entities/topics/events)
High consensus-cluster alignment with centroid proximity
Format-valid, mutually distinct tag sets
Fast task turnaround across topic seasons
entries.top10Strategy: Consensus is king: 60% of a tag's score is alignment with the dominant cluster, so tags matching how other good miners read the post win, while the diversity term punishes redundancy within your own set. Prompt for the obvious tags plus one distinctive angle, and never copy others' exact sets - the duplicate penalty is sigmoid-steep. Track whitelist account styles as topic seasons rotate.
top10Levers: Consensus-aligned tagging (0.6 weight on cluster support)
Distinct tags within your own set (diversity weight 0.4)
Prompt engineering for tier-1.0 format validity
Cheap model choice with semantic quality (OpenAI overrides)
Docker auto-update to track scoring changes
entries.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnets/101 top UIDs, tag101-ai/tag101 commits (scoring formulas and whitelist evolve), and in-repo topic-season announcements.

entries.name: ReadyAI
entries.whatItDoes: ReadyAI is a decentralized data-structuring pipeline: miners use LLM APIs to turn raw conversations, webpages, surveys, and documents into structured tags, entities, and embeddings for vector databases. Validators fully tag the same data as ground truth and score miner tags by embedding cosine distance. Businesses buy the structured output, published toward HuggingFace datasets.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU only: 8GB+ RAM, 20GB+ disk. No local GPU - annotation runs through OpenAI (GPT-4o default), Anthropic, groq, OpenRouter or Chutes APIs at the miner's cost. RunPod cheap CPU instances are explicitly supported with a launch template.
keyRequirements: OpenAI API key (GPT-4o default) plus a Weights & Biases key required
CPU with 8GB+ RAM and 20GB+ disk; axon port must be reachable
Registered hotkey; Dockerized deploy or Runpod CPU template both supported
Tag quality scored by cosine distance to validator ground-truth tags
LLM API spend is miner-billed, so margin management is core
entries.minerJob: Run neurons/miner.py (or the Runpod template): the axon receives TaskBundles - conversation windows, webpage markdown, surveys, skill documents - calls your configured LLM to emit topical tags plus embeddings, and returns them. Validators tag the same windows as ground truth and score each miner tag by cosine distance to the truth neighborhood; selected miners per window earn, feeding EMA and on-chain weights. Task types include named-entity extraction and skill generation.
minerJobProvide: Flat tag lists plus embeddings for conversation/webpage/survey windows
Normalized named-entity extractions from documents and transcripts
LLM skill-generation documents for skill_coverage_evaluation tasks
Cheap, accurate GPT-4o-class annotation at scale
entries.top10Strategy: This is a margin game: reward minus API cost. Winners tune prompts so tag style matches the validator's ground-truth conventions, prune redundant tags, and pick the cheapest capable model per task type. Only a few miners are selected per window, so responsiveness and uptime count. Newcomers: replicate the reference miner first, then optimize prompt and model cost per tag until margin is positive.
top10Levers: Prompt engineering aligned with ground-truth tagging style
Embedding closeness to validator ground truth
Uptime - only selected miners earn per window
Runpod CPU template for cheap hosting
entries.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnets/33 top UIDs and reward spread, repo commit cadence (new task types shift scoring), and the Bittensor Discord subnet-33 channel.

entries.name: MVTRX
entries.whatItDoes: MVTRX/τaos runs an agent-based market simulation: miners host trading strategies inside a C++ limit-order-book simulator with L3 data and background agents, scored on intraday Kappa-3 (risk-adjusted) with minimum trading volume. Optional GenTRX adds distributed training of a shared order-book generative model (~5% pool). An alpha-token exchange is a later release.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU-only for trading: no set requirements; base tooling ~1GB RAM per miner instance (VPS works). Optional NVIDIA 6-8GB VRAM GPU for GenTRX training; CPU-only training supported but may miss deadlines. No GPU for the main 95% pool.
keyRequirements: Custom agent class loaded from ~/.taos/agents (subclass GenTRXAgent for training opt-in)
Respond to every state-update tick; response latency sets execution slippage
Maintain minimum cumulative round-trip volume for full scoring
Rolling-window scores persist across weekly simulation configurations
GenTRX: S3 bucket for compressed gradient uploads
entries.minerJob: Your agent receives L3 order-book state updates from validators each tick and returns place/cancel instructions; the simulation pauses while awaiting you, and your response time determines the delay (slippage) applied to your orders. Scores use intraday Kappa-3 plus activity requirements, on a rolling window across runs that reset weekly. GenTRX opt-in trains the shared model on your assigned data slice in a background thread and uploads compressed gradients to a personal S3 bucket for validator scoring (~95/5 pool split).
minerJobProvide: Trading-agent order instructions per state tick
Risk-managed positive Kappa-3 across market realizations
Minimum round-trip volume maintenance
GenTRX gradients (optional) on schedule
entries.top10Strategy: A pure quant-skill war: market-making with tight risk control, fast responses to minimize slippage, and strategies robust to weekly re-parameterized markets. Newcomers: start from example agents, backtest offline against the local proxy background model, then layer GenTRX for the extra training pool with zero trade-off against trading rewards.
entries.followTopMiners: Watch the Grafana dashboards (taos.simulate.trading, mvtrx.simulate.trading), taostats.io/subnet/79 for weights, the repo's agents/ directory and config releases, and the taos Discord for parameter-change announcements.

entries.name: Desearch
entries.whatItDoes: Desearch builds a pre-query web index for AI on Bittensor. In the live 2.0 phase miners crawl assigned pages and upload extracted text; validators re-check a sample under published rules; the Desearch team integrates accepted pages into the index behind its Search API (console.desearch.ai). Miners are paid by their share of accepted pages. Embedding tasks are built and open later.
entries.hardwareRec: CPU-only for the crawl phase: any cheap VPS with bandwidth and disk. The later embed program will pay miners to run the selected embedding model on GPUs, so keep a modest GPU option in mind. Rentals fine.
keyRequirements: Registered hotkey on SN22 + task API access (docs/miner-setup.md)
Fetch assigned pages and upload extracted text
Validators re-fetch random samples; mismatch forfeits earnings since last good check
All results public at api-22.desearch.ai/v1/tasks
Local miner test before registering (test-your-miner.md)
entries.minerJob: The miner takes tasks from the task API, fetches its assigned URLs, extracts clean text, and uploads it for the index. Validators re-fetch a random sample of each miner's tasks and compare; weights are set from the share of accepted work, and a miner caught returning bad pages loses everything earned since its last good check. A future embed task type will run a selected model on accepted text with sample recomputation. Reward = your share of accepted pages per round.
minerJobProvide: Fetched page text for assigned URLs
Extraction fidelity matching validator re-fetch
High accepted-page share per round
Later: embeddings from the selected model
entries.top10Strategy: A crawl-reliability war: fetch success rate on hard pages, extraction accuracy, and throughput decide your accepted share. Newcomers: run the reference miner, pass the local validator test first, then tune concurrency and IP quality. Never shortcut pages — sampling makes cheating lose everything since the last good check.
top10Levers: Fetch success rate on assigned pages
Fast adoption of new task types (embed)
entries.followTopMiners: Watch the public task log api-22.desearch.ai/v1/tasks, docs/emission.md for share mechanics, taostats.io/subnet/22 for incentive distribution, and the Desearch Discord/X for program openings (embedding phase).

entries.name: ItsAI
entries.whatItDoes: It's AI (SN32) is a decentralized AI-text detector: miners run detection models that classify text as human-written or AI-generated, including per-sentence 'deep scan' probabilities. Validators continuously query miners with human and AI texts generated by 30+ LLMs under varied parameters, augmentations, and adversarial attacks. The team monetizes detection via its-ai.org, API, and extensions.
entries.hardwareRec: 1x RTX 4090 24GB (input metadata; platform engine rates it container-friendly with no TEE/bare-metal/static-IP requirement - rented GPUs work). Detector inference fits comfortably in 24GB; keep latency low.
keyRequirements: Registered hotkey plus subnet registration burn (~0.058 TAO per platform snapshot)
24GB-class GPU serving the detector model behind your axon
Robust accuracy across 30+ generator LLMs, augmentations, adversarial attacks
Low false-positive rate (education buyers care)
Container/rented hosting fine; deep validator pool queries regularly
entries.minerJob: You serve an AI-detection model on your axon. Validators stream human-written and AI-generated texts (from top LLM-arena models with varied generation params, augmentations, and adversarial attacks) and score your classifications; per-sentence deep-scan probabilities are part of the product surface. The incentive mechanism is time-proven - the team reports SOTA on MGTD, RAID (98.3% accuracy), and GRiD/HC3/GhostBuster benchmarks, and credits the incentive design for keeping miners improving rather than gaming. Platform snapshots show a wide reward distribution (239/256 miners earned; ~94% rewarded ratio), so reliable mid-tier accuracy still pays while top accuracy takes the largest weights.
minerJobProvide: Human-vs-AI text classification
Per-sentence AI-probability deep scan
Low false-positive classification on human text
Fast, always-on inference endpoint
entries.top10Strategy: Push benchmark-grade accuracy: retrain regularly on fresh generator LLMs, harden against paraphrase/attack augmentations, and control FPR. Small accuracy edges pay continuously because validators query all day and the reward pool is broad. Match the published incentive doc's direction (it produced their SOTA), keep inference fast, and watch benchmark leaderboards as your north star.
top10Levers: Retraining cadence tied to docs/incentive.md updates
entries.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnet/32 incentive distribution (broad, ~94% rewarded) and top-UID accuracy churn; its-ai.org/en/accuracy reports; MGTD/RAID leaderboards; repo docs/incentive.md changes; Bittensor Discord SN32 channels.
